items.stem: A teacher runs student work through an AI-detection tool that flags an essay. What is the most responsible response?

options.text: Treat the flag as one uncertain signal, not proof, and investigate fairly
options.rationale: Correct: AI detectors are unreliable and can produce false positives.

options.text: Automatically fail the student based on the flag
options.rationale: Acting on an unreliable flag alone is unfair.
Integrity still matters; the issue is how to assess it fairly.

items.explanation: Correct: AI detectors are unreliable and can produce false positives.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices help keep AI use in a classroom equitable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Provide an alternative for students without AI access
options.rationale: Correct: alternatives prevent access gaps from harming learners.

options.text: Check AI materials for bias before sharing them
options.rationale: Correct: reviewing for bias protects fairness.

options.text: Require every student to buy a paid AI subscription
options.rationale: Mandating paid tools creates an equity barrier.

options.text: Assume all AI output is culturally neutral
options.rationale: AI output can carry bias and gaps.

items.explanation: Correct: alternatives prevent access gaps from harming learners.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An AI tool writes a history explanation for a lesson. Before teaching it, the educator should mainly:

options.text: Verify the facts and framing for accuracy and balance
options.rationale: Correct: AI can introduce factual errors or skewed framing.

options.text: Teach it verbatim to save time
Assume historical facts are always correct in AI output
Add more detail without checking any of it
options.rationale: More unchecked detail compounds the risk.

items.explanation: Correct: AI can introduce factual errors or skewed framing.
